Commentary.Commentary: Just three batsmen entered double figures for Papua New Guinea. Lega Siaka scored 39 but Jason Kila's 27 in 11 balls might have just given the Berrandis some much-needed momentum. Remember, a day ago, Namibia struggled to chase down a total around 130? 22 runs came in the final over. That might just be the margin of defeat for the Dutch as well. Stay tuned...

Brandon Glover says that it started a bit shaky but only focused on what he needed to do. Adds that he used the short ball as a surprise, concentrating on bowling yorkers. On him running hard, Brandon says that night games do help you a touch. Backs his team to chase the total down.

The begin was excellent from the Orange team. Roelof van der Merwe got a wicket in the very first over and PNG never really got back in. He ended up with 2/15 while Timm van der Gugten got a couple as well. Brandon Glover was the pick of the bowlers though, with 3/24 in his 4 overs. His pace and bounce surprised everyone and PNG had no idea how to play him. Here he is, talking to Robert Key.
Wow. Has that last lover snatched the title away from the Dutch? It was an excellent piece of controlled bowling by the Netherlands till then, before Jason Kila came along...

Good length delivery outside off, Kila looks to go big but misses it. It goes towards Scott Edwards who fires a throw at the bowler's end and the batsmen steal a bye. 22 runs have come off the final over. PAPUA NEW GUINEA FINISH ON 128/8!
On a good length and outside off, Kila shoulders arms to this one.

FOUR! It is already 21 runs off the first 4 balls. On a good length and outside off, Kila looks to slog but gets an outside edge. It goes over Scott Edwards who jumps to catch it towards third man for a boundary.
FOUR! 17 runs have already come off the first three balls. Short and outside off, Kila cuts it over point for a boundary.
WIDE! Full delivery wide outside off, Kila looks to drive but misses it.
SIX! Excellent shot. This is on the pads again and Kila swings it cleanly in front of square leg this time!
SIX! Nicely done! A length ball, down the leg side, Kila swings it over square leg!
Paul van Meekeren is back on. 3-0-13-0 are his figures so far.
On a length on middle, Kila flicks it through mid-wicket. The batsmen take a run. 4 runs and a wicket from the over. This is good death bowling by Netherlands.
Nosaina Pokana is the new batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT! This is poor batting by Papua New Guinea. Short of a length delivery, Hekure looks to pull but gets a top edge. It goes towards square leg where the keeper Scott Edwards runs forward and takes a good catch.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
A length ball outside off, Kila looks to swing but drags it through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A slower ball, around middle, pulled through square leg for a single.
Riely Hekure walks in at number 9, replacing Bau.

OUT! CAUGHT! Glover bowls a short of a length delivery on leg, Bau looks to pull but gets a faint edge off the gloves. It goes towards Scott Edwards who takes a comfortable catch. This is good bowling by Netherlands. 6 runs and 2 wickets from the over.
Short delivery, Bau looks to pull but misses it.
Full again on off, Kila drives it through covers where Ben Cooper tries to stop it but it goes through him. The batsmen get three runs. Good running between the wickets. 100 up for Papua New Guinea.

Full toss on leg, Kila looks to flick but misses it and gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head. It goes towards the leg side. The batsmen cross ends. The umpire gives it as a leg bye.
WIDE! Bowls it down the leg side, Bau leaves it alone.
On a length on middle, Kila flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a run.
Jason Kila is the new batsman in.
OUT! BOWLED! Glover bowls it on a good length on leg, Vanua looks to pull but misses it completely and gets bowled. Papua New Guinea are in deep trouble here. They have lost their sixth wicket.
Glover is back on. 3-0-19-1 are his figures so far.

Short delivery outside off, Vanua cuts it through point. The batsmen take a single.
Oh dear. Short and well outside off, slow in pace too. Vanua waits and waits and waits before slashing hard. But still misses.

On a good length and outside off, Bau looks to swing at this one but misses it.
Full delivery on off, Bau looks to drive but gets a bottom edge on this one.

Short delivery on middle, Vanua pulls it through mid-wicket. The batsmen take a single.

OUT! That is a stunning catch! Scott Edwards has pulled off an absolute blinder. A short ball, outside off, Doriga looks to steer it to third man, or rather, play the upper cut. But the ball suddenly bounces and then cramps him for room. Doriga is caught by surprise but cannot do anything. He is caught in no man's land and the ball just flies off the outside edge behind. But so does the keeper. Edwards keeps his eyes on the ball, leaps to his right and takes it two-handed.
BEATEN! Bowls a short ball outside off, Doriga looks to play an upper cut but misses it.
Good length delivery on middle, Doriga looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a good length on middle, Bau looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It goes towards the off side. The batsmen take a single.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Full and outside off, Bau comes down the track and drives it through covers for a boundary.

OUT! TIMBER! Flighted delivery on middle, Siaka looks to go for a lofted shot but misses it and gets bowled. Papua New Guinea lose their fourth wicket. They need a big partnership coming their way.

Comes down the track and works it through mid on for a couple.
Full and around middle, pushed back towards mid on.

Flighted delivery on off, Siaka punches it towards point for a single.
SIX! Amazing shot. Short delivery on middle, Siaka pulls it over mid-wicket for a maximum.

Landed outside off, pushed through point for a single.

On a length on middle, Siaka nudges it towards square leg for a single.

BEATEN! On a good length and outside off, Bau looks to cut but misses it. Papua New Guinea are 30/3 after 6 overs. It has been an excellent Powerplay for Netherlands.

OUT! CAUGHT! Netherlands get their third breakthrough. Van der Gugten bowls a slower ball outside off, Amini looks to loft it over mid off but gets early into the shot. It goes off the toe end of his bat towards mid off where Ben Cooper takes the simplest of catches. Gone for a duck.

OUT! Vala is run out! The skipper is gone. Well, what a bonus for Netherlands but this is something which they have earned. A length ball, down the leg side, Assad looks to tuck it to the leg side and does so, albeit off the bottom half of the bat. The ball goes straight to short fine leg but Vala sets off for a run. He is halfway down by the time he looks up at his partner who has already sent him back. Vala sets off to do a u-turn but Tobias Visee at short fine, collects, takes aim and fires. Bull's eye. The stumps are hit at the keeper's end and Vala is declared out. Replays show that he just fell short by an inch but was short.
Full and around middle, dug out back to the bowler.
FOUR! BLUDGEONED! Intent. A length ball outside off, Vala jumps down the track, converts the length ball into a fuller one and smashes it over cover. One bounce and into the fence.
A length ball, around middle, extra bounce, Vala hops and plays it towards point.

FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Siaka. Flighted delivery on middle, Siaka comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

FOUR! Leg byes or runs? The latter signalled. Tossed up delivery on leg, spinning down, Siaka looks to flick but misses it. The ball goes off his pads, past the keeper, to the fine leg fence but still, runs given. Siaka won't mind.

FIVE WIDES! Nerves. And plenty of them. Glover comes around the wicket and bowls a poor delivery down the leg side. It pitches and then swings further down, beating Vala's attempted pull. The keeper dives to his right, full stretch, but cannot get anywhere near it.

Paul van Meekeren to bowl from the other end.

An arm ball again, fired in around middle, Siaka goes back to tuck it to the leg side but misses and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. A frugal opening over, with a wicket to boot. It is like getting bread at a cheap rate and soup to go with it, free of cost.
Lega Siaka comes in at number 3, replacing Ura.

OUT! LBW! Plumb in front. Ura has to go. This is what happens when you attack and just attack. It is like walking on a thin rope. You live by the sword and die by it. So, the ball is straight. You look to hit. Then hit it. If you don't, then better go. So van der Merwe keeps this very straight, just around off and gets it to come in with the arm. Tony gets down to sweep, just like he did a couple of balls ago. But, misses. Trouble. Appeal. Scream. Slow death. The umpire takes his time but eventually raises his finger.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! BLAST! He has just faced one ball and is off. Full and around middle, coming in with the arm, Ura gets down and slogs it behind square leg for a boundary!
Around middle, punched towards mid on.
Around off, coming in, worked towards short mid-wicket for a single.

The players are out in the middle. Tony Ura and Assad Vala are the openers for the Barramundis (A new word learnt today). Roelof van der Merwe will start off proceedings to the PNG skipper. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - What is this pitch going to do? It has been a high-scoring venue in this tournament but not so in the last 2 games. Because of the abrasiveness of the surface. Dirk Nannes feels that this is a levelling surface, with the quicks getting pace and bounce and the spinners getting turn.

Netherlands captain, Pieter Seelaar admits that batting first would have been Netherlands' preference but now, wants his bowling unit to restrict Papua New Guinea to a chaseable total. Is happy that his spinners have done well in this tournament but also says that they have been growing for a long time now. On the team changes, Seelaar feels that the Dutch have a strong middle order but informs that they have gone in with Tobias Visee tonight, who can score some quick runs. On the weather, Pieter is happy to be playing at this time of the night, as it is a bit cooler. Ian Bishop asks Seelaar again about the change, as the incoming guy was mentioned, but now, Pieter says that Visee has come in for Fred Klaassen.

Papua New Guinea skipper, Assad Vala, says that the reason for batting first is because that formula has given them recent success and most of the teams have been winning by batting first. Is really happy to have come this far and is looking forward to the final challenge. Feels that adapting to the wickets has been his team's main reason for success and hopes for more of the same tonight.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Max O'Dowd, Tobias Visee (IN FOR FRED KLAASSEN), Ben Cooper, Colin Ackermann, Ryan ten Doeschate, Pieter Seelaar(C), Roelof van der Merwe, Scott Edwards(WK), Timm van der Gugten, Brandon Glover and Paul van Meekeren.
Papua New Guinea (UNCHANGED Playing XI) - Tony Ura, Assad Vala (C), Lega Siaka, Charles Amini, Sese Bau, Kiplin Doriga (WK), Norman Vanua, Riley Hekure, Jason Kila, Damien Ravu and Nosaina Pokana.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Papua New Guinea. PAPUA NEW GUINEA HAVE ELECTED TO BAT FIRST.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final of the T20 World Cup Qualifier between Netherlands and Papua New Guinea in Dubai. Both the teams will look to play an exciting final. Netherlands would look to continue their strong performance tonight and look to win the T20 Qualifiers. They would want their batting to come good and do well. On the other hand, Papua New Guinea have a good bowling attack and have defended low totals in this tournament. They would look to give a tough fight to Netherlands. Stay tuned for the toss.
